newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani interbank market rates crash.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani interbank market rates crash.

text.p: Pakistan's interbank money market rates crashed on Thursday on an inflow of funds, dealers said.
The year dawned with chances of interest rates easing from last year's close at 20 percent because of the day's inflows, at dealer at the KASB & Co said.
However, with desperate borrowing at 19.50 percent, early morning rates failed to ease off, he said. It was towards the end of the day that bids suddenly crashed and fell to 10 percent.

"Trading was conducted between 9.0 and 11 percent and the day ended with banks squaring off their positions at the 2.0 and 3.0 percent mark," the dealer said. "The magnitude of the inflow took banks by surprise and caused short-term rates to crash at the end of the day."

"We are of the opinion that the market is expected to remain at these rock bottom levels and conditions could only take a turn if the State (central) Bank of Pakistan continues its policy of conducting open market operations from early next week," the dealer said. -- Ibrahim Khan 9221-5685192
